summary: Iteration 6 (per-platform conversion tracking for Apple Watch vs Wear OS) fully verified — backend 22/22 pytest cases pass (9 new platform-focused tests added), frontend Playwright flow validates all 13 review-request items end-to-end at 1440x900 and 375x812. POST /api/waitlist accepts platform, coerces unknown values (windows) to null without 422, forces platform=null when audience!=watch, idempotency is now keyed on (email, audience, platform) so watch+apple and watch+android produce two distinct records. GET /api/waitlist/count returns expanded shape {count, watch_apple, watch_android} with non-negative ints and watch_apple+watch_android<=count. Tailored email subjects 'Welcome to the Wrist beta — Apple Watch edition' and '— Wear OS edition' verified via direct render. Frontend: wearable-platform-apple/android chips are clickable buttons that set audience='watch' + platform + smooth-scroll to #cta. CTA cta-platform-picker is visible only when audience=='watch', supports single-select toggle with deselect via re-click, helper line cta-platform-detail reads exactly 'Tailored for Apple Watch · watchOS.' or 'Tailored for Wear OS · Galaxy / Pixel.'. Switching audience to 'kids' hides the picker AND resets platform to null (verified: returning to watch shows neither chip selected). Toast labels confirmed mid-flight via polling: 'You're on the Wrist beta (Apple Watch) list.', '(Wear OS) list.', and generic 'Wrist beta list.' when no platform. wearable-cta still works without platform. Regression: nav (Pillars/Experience/Wearable/Pricing) intact, modules=4, usecases tabs=4 (testid usecases-tab-*), pricing tiers=4, FAQ=6. 0 console errors, 0 page errors.

critical_code_review_comments: audienceStore.js: clean encapsulation — useSyncExternalStore with combined snapshot 'audience|platform' correctly drives re-renders on either change. setAudience() clears _platform when audience!='watch' — this is the single source of truth that backs the FE-side reset behaviour observed in tests.
CTA.jsx L141: cta-platform-picker is correctly mounted only when audience==='watch', and the platform sub-picker uses single-select toggle (sel ? null : key). Good UX.
CTA.jsx L37-38: outgoing POST payload defensively forces platform=null when audience!=='watch'. Belt-and-suspenders since backend also enforces this — safe.

CTA.jsx L42-43: toast label construction is correct — only labels (Apple Watch)/(Wear OS) when audience==='watch' AND platform is set. The 'no platform' watch case correctly falls back to plain 'Wrist beta' label.

server.py L196-218: idempotency now keyed on (email, audience, platform) which is the desired iteration-6 behaviour. Backfill of legacy records via existing.setdefault('platform', None) is a thoughtful touch for records that pre-date this iteration.
server.py L203-206: platform whitelisted to {'apple','android'}, then force-nulled when audience!='watch'. Invalid values are coerced (not 422'd) — matches spec.
server.py L246-251: count endpoint shape expanded with two cheap count_documents queries. Could be slow at scale but is correct and matches spec.
Wearable.jsx: redundant scroll calls when platform chip is clicked (Wearable does an explicit scrollIntoView and CTA.jsx's useEffect would also scroll on audience change). Harmless but worth noting.

Pre-existing (unchanged): server.py defines logger AFTER _send_confirmation_email which references it. Works because logger is module-level by the time the function is called at runtime, but stylistically should move logging setup above its first usage. Not a blocker.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 6 adds per-platform tracking on top of iteration 5. Store now returns 4-tuple [audience, setAudience, platform, setPlatform]. cta-platform-picker only renders when audience==='watch'. Backend POST /api/waitlist now accepts optional platform; idempotency is keyed on (email, audience, platform). GET /api/waitlist/count shape changed from {count} → {count, watch_apple, watch_android}. Email templates have a platform-specific branch (apple/android) layered above the audience-specific one. Sonner toasts auto-dismiss in ~4s — to capture toast text in Playwright, poll within ~8s of the submit click (see test 2 in the test report for the polling pattern). Run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_waitlist.py -v`.
